headline: Wall Street bought the vote but sold the AI build: the Dow had its best day since April 2025 while power, cooling and chip suppliers fell on data center limits, oil dropped almost 10% and stopped out all four oil swings, and the Bank of England hiked to 4%.
summary: The dashboard is two days behind: prices_as_of is 2026-11-03 and the Nov 4 close is missing, so every Nov 4 level here comes from Massive. On Wednesday SPY rose 1.65% to 766.81, DIA 3.10% and QQQ 0.97% to 691.95, which puts QQQ 8.9% under its Oct 6 record and back above the 10% correction line. Under the surface it was a rotation: the AI buyers rose (Microsoft 6.68%, Amazon 6.12%) while the AI suppliers fell on fears of data center limits after Texas elected a governor who wants a pause (Vistra 13.83%, Vertiv 12.89%, CoreWeave 9.90%). Brent settled down 9.73% at $93.52, and XOM, CVX, COP and EOG all hit their swing stops. Copom held at 13.75% last night and the Bank of England raised to 4.00% this morning; futures are mixed, with chips down again. The put screen passes nothing: MSFT, PFE and CHKP ran above their zones, APH fell back in but its chart broke, and the other puts barely trade.

regime.why: The vote removed an unknown and the broad market rallied, but money left the AI build that has led this market, oil is swinging 10% a day on Iran headlines, and central banks abroad are still hiking. Nasdaq 100 futures were down 0.7% before the open. Friday's jobs report is the next test.

signals.title: The day after the vote: buyers of AI rose, sellers to AI fell
signals.since_yesterday: The futures pop held: the Dow closed up 3.03%, its best day since April 2025, and QQQ ended 8.9% under its record, back above the 10% correction line.
signals.what_happened: Nov 4 closes (Massive): SPY 766.81 (+1.65%), DIA 533.11 (+3.10%), QQQ 691.95 (+0.97%), IWM 284.02 (+1.51%), SMH 504.27 (-2.75%). Microsoft rose 6.68% to 555.80, Amazon 6.12% and Apple 5.31%, while Nvidia fell 3.17%. Forbes and CNBC say investors bet a Democratic Congress cools the AI spending race. The 10 year yield closed near 4.89% (Investing.com). Before the open Thursday, Dow futures were up about 0.5%, S&P 500 futures flat and Nasdaq 100 futures down about 0.7%, with the chip ETF down more than 3% (Yahoo, Bloomberg).
signals.so_what: Follow the money: the hyperscalers pay for the AI build, and the suppliers get paid. If permits slow the build, the payers keep more cash (good for MSFT and AMZN free cash flow) and the suppliers lose orders. That is why the same news lifted Microsoft and sank Vistra. Third order: data centers that are already built and powered become scarcer and may charge more. What would make this wrong: the hyperscalers say on their next calls that spending plans are unchanged.
signals.for_you: Swing: no setups on the dashboard (Nov 3 closes); a broad rally on a split tape is not a breakout. Long term: MSFT closed 555.80, 5% above the top of its 424.32 to 529.48 zone, so it is no longer a buy now name; no chasing. Puts: the bar is the 4.89% 10 year.

signals.title: Data center limits: AI power, cooling and neoclouds sell off; Korea follows
signals.what_happened: Texas elected Democrat Gina Hinojosa as governor; she campaigned on a pause for new data centers, and some Democrats in Congress want a national pause until rules are set or want tech firms to pay more of the power bill (CNBC, Yahoo). Goldman estimates state moratoriums could put about 45% of planned US data center capacity at risk, UBS about 30% of 2028 additions, and Wells Fargo says Texas holds about 27% of planned capacity. Nov 4 closes (Massive): Vistra -13.83%, Vertiv -12.89%, Eaton -9.86%, GE Vernova -9.30%, Constellation -6.71%, CoreWeave -9.90%, Nebius -6.67%. In Seoul the KOSPI fell 5.28% to 5,383.80 on Nov 5, with SK hynix down 9.46% and Samsung 7.57% (Korea Exchange via FN News), while Hong Kong tech rose about 5.6% as money rotated into Chinese internet names (Bloomberg).
signals.so_what: The scarce thing may be changing from power to permits. Power plant owners in Texas sold off hardest because a pause would cut the new demand they priced in. But the facts so far are a campaign promise, not a law: Texas still has a Republican legislature, Vistra had hedged about 94% of its 2027 output, and Vertiv's orders more than doubled last quarter (Yahoo). Heavy volume on the way down is distribution, so expect more selling before a floor. What would make this wrong: the governor-elect softens the pause into fees or rules.
signals.for_you: Swing: no buys in VST, VRT, ETN, GEV, CEG, CRWV or NBIS until a base forms. Puts: none in the AI power group while it falls; premiums look rich because risk is real. Vistra reports Friday, Nov 6. Long term: none of these has a buy verdict. Watch MSFT and AMZN for a pullback into their zones instead.

signals.title: Oil falls almost 10% on deal bets; all four oil swings hit their stops
signals.since_yesterday: Brent settled down 9.73% at $93.52 on Nov 4, and XOM, CVX, COP and EOG all traded through their stops (Massive).
signals.what_happened: Brent's January contract fell $10.08 to $93.52, the lowest settle since Aug 31, and traded near $94 early Thursday (FinanceFeeds). One report says the US approved a Qatar draft memorandum in which Iran would make a nuclear concession for some frozen funds; Iran's security council secretary called the US reply 'not convincing', and Tehran says Hormuz stays shut until its conditions are met (HNGN, Korea Herald). Nov 4 (Massive): XOM low 167.39, close 169.27 (stop 169.99). CVX low 214.61, close 216.96 (stop 218.23). COP low 134.72, close 136.94 (stop 135.75). EOG low 146.31, close 147.06 (stop 147.98). USO fell 8.07% and XLE 4.74%.
signals.so_what: Markets are pricing a deal that is not signed. That is the risk both ways: oil can jump back if talks stall, or fall further if Hormuz opens. Who pays: producers and Gulf budgets. Who gets paid: airlines, shippers, consumers, and central banks that get some relief on inflation. Raising the XOM and CVX stops to the entries did its job: the plans closed near breakeven instead of giving back more.
signals.for_you: Swing: the XOM, CVX, COP and EOG plans are closed by the stop rule (XOM and CVX near the 169.99 and 218.23 entries; COP and EOG at their stops). No re-entry until oil bases and a fresh setup appears on the dashboard. Puts: none on energy.

signals.title: Hospitals and medtech rally on Medicaid hopes; Novo's pill beats; Zoetis beats
signals.since_yesterday: The premarket pop in hospitals and Medicaid insurers held into the close and spread to device makers.
signals.what_happened: Nov 4 closes (Massive): HCA +10.34%, Tenet +9.58%, Centene +12.64%, Molina +8.93%, Intuitive Surgical +9.38% to 482.10, Stryker +9.37%, Dexcom +6.64%, Insulet +6.56% and Medtronic +6.15%. Analysts said a Democratic Congress could delay Medicaid enrollment cuts from last year's budget law (Investrade, Investing.com). Novo Nordisk's Wegovy pill sold DKK 5.39 billion in Q3 against DKK 4.62 billion expected; it raised guidance and will cut US list prices for Wegovy and Ozempic to $675 a month on Jan 1 (CNBC); NVO rose 4.95%. Zoetis this morning: revenue $2.39 billion, down 1%, US down 6%; adjusted EPS $1.75 against $1.51 expected by Zacks; full year adjusted EPS guidance raised to $6.25 to $6.35 (AP, company release).
signals.so_what: For a clinician the link is simple: more people covered means more procedures and fewer unpaid bills, which helps hospitals first and procedure device makers next. But the law is not changed yet, and the new Congress starts in January. Zoetis shows the US pet business is still soft even as earnings beat. The pill is pulling patients from shots, so GLP-1 volume keeps rising while price per patient falls.
signals.for_you: Long term: PODD (165.02) and MDT (104.96) stay 'Accumulate on pullback'; MDT is well above its 84.35 to 94.36 zone. No chasing a one day policy pop. Swing: TMO showed up on her MT Swing Setup scan (see inbox), but the dashboard has no setup yet.

signals.title: Central banks: Copom ends its cuts, the Bank of England hikes, jobs Friday
signals.since_yesterday: Both decisions are in: Copom held at 13.75% and the Bank of England raised to 4.00%.
signals.what_happened: Copom held the Selic at 13.75% unanimously on Nov 4 and ended the cuts that began in March; 72 of 105 institutions expected a hold and 33 a cut (Poder360, Sou Brasilia). The Bank of England raised Bank Rate 0.25 point to 4.00% at 7am ET today, 8 to 1, with one vote for 4.25%; it tied the move to energy costs, and the next decision is Dec 17 (Bank of England). US October jobs come Friday at 8:30am ET: the Dow Jones consensus is 59,000 with unemployment at 4.2% (Kiplinger); FactSet has 65,000, and ADP showed 86,000 private jobs (US News).
signals.so_what: The Bank of England hiked even though oil just fell 10%. Central banks are still fighting inflation that has spread from energy into other prices. That keeps long rates high and caps how far growth stocks can rerate. A strong jobs number would push the Fed toward a December hike.
signals.for_you: No action. No Brazil or UK trades. Avoid opening new swings Friday morning before 8:30am ET.

cycle.quadrant: Growth rising and inflation rising (overheating), with inflation pressure easing at the margin
cycle.quadrant_why: Q3 GDP grew at a 3.4% pace and core PCE was 3.1% (Oct 29 data, unchanged). Brent fell almost 10% to $93.52 on Nov 4, which eases the inflation side if it lasts. ADP showed 86,000 private jobs in October; Friday's report is the next growth read.
cycle.short_term_debt_cycle: Tightening, late. The Bank of England hiked to 4.00% today, Brazil stopped cutting at 13.75%, and the Fed (3.75% to 4.00% since Oct 28) is weighing a December hike. The 10 year closed near 4.89%.
cycle.long_term_debt_cycle: Late. US debt is above $40 trillion. A split government makes new spending harder, which bond buyers liked, but it also raises shutdown risk next year.
cycle.big_cycle: Internal order: power is now split, and state level politics (Texas) can now slow the AI build. External order: US and Iran talks through Qatar drive a 10% oil swing in a day. Technology: AI demand is still strong (Coherent, AMD), but the build now faces a permit and politics risk it did not have last week.
tailwinds: Oil fell almost 10%, which eases inflation if it holds.
The broad market rallied; QQQ is back above the 10% correction line.
AI demand is still visible in supplier results (Coherent up 79% in data center).
headwinds: Data center limits are now a real policy risk for the AI build.
Central banks abroad are still hiking.
The Iran deal is not signed, so oil can swing back fast.

history.what: Oil had its biggest one day drop on record when early reports showed the allies winning: WTI fell about 33%, from $32.25 to $21.48 (Oil and Gas Journal). Stocks and bonds rallied the same day (Bank of England Quarterly Bulletin).
history.lesson: A war premium can vanish in a day once the market sees an end, and the people long oil get no warning.
